– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testRfc4648Section10Encode` expects the Base64 encoding of the string "f" to be "Zg==". This encoding result generally does not require chunking (insertion of line breaks).

From the current bug report and the code snippet of `Base64.encodeBase64String(byte[] binaryData)`, the method calls `encodeBase64(binaryData, true)`, which indicates chunking is enabled. This could cause the encoded output to be split by inserted line breaks, which is incorrect for such short input data and also not expected per the test.

The method `encodeBase64(byte[] binaryData, boolean isChunked)` calls `encodeBase64(byte[] binaryData, boolean isChunked, boolean urlSafe)` which calls the most detailed form `encodeBase64(byte[] binaryData, boolean isChunked, boolean urlSafe, int maxResultSize)`.

Inside this most detailed encode method, when `isChunked` is true, a new Base64 encoder is created with default chunking settings (constructor `new Base64(urlSafe)`), which apparently enables chunking. However, when `isChunked` is false, the `Base64` is constructed by `new Base64(0, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe)` disabling chunking (lineLength=0 disables chunking).

The current implementation of `encodeBase64String` uses `encodeBase64(binaryData, true)` resulting in chunking enabled, which can lead to unwanted line breaks in the encoded string even with small input.

This behavior contradicts the expected output in the test. The bug report suggests a fix by changing `true` to `false` in `encodeBase64String()`, disabling chunking and hence preventing encoding from inserting line breaks.

Recent bug reports also indicate changes in the default behaviour of Base64 encoding related to chunking, confirming that the core issue is related to chunking enabled by default.

Therefore, the root cause of the test failure is that `Base64.encodeBase64String()` wrongly enables chunking, causing inserted line breaks that invalidate the expected output.

Suggested fix: Change the call inside `encodeBase64String` from `encodeBase64(binaryData, true)` to `encodeBase64(binaryData, false)`, disabling line chunking on encoding the base64 string, which will align with tests and RFC 4648 section 10 expected outputs.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
